articles.title: Lon Lon Ranch Super Cuccos Mini-Game - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Super Cuccos is a Mini-Game found in Lon Lon Ranch in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. This mini-game requires you to pick three super cuccos out
articles.body:
Super Cuccos is a Mini-Game found in Lon Lon Ranch in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. This mini-game requires you to pick three super cuccos out of a room full of cuccos within a set time limit.

Check out IGN's full guide to Super Cuccos below.

The Super Cucco game is found in the house at Lon Lon Ranch, during the day. Speak to Talon is asleep amid the pile of chickens, speak to him to take on the challenge.

To win, find all three of his "Super Cuccos" amid the gaggle of other Cuccos in the room. The trick to finding them is to pay close attention to the mannerisms of the Super Cuccos. Compared to the regular ones, they are stiff and upright, wings angled down, and holding their heads high and flapping dramatically on occasion.

Win, and you'll get yourself a second Empty Bottle, filled with Lon Lon Milk by default.

Up Next: Castle Town Shooting Gallery Mini-Game

articles.title: Lake Hylia Fishing Pond Mini-Game - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Fishing Pond is a Mini-Game found in Lake Hylia in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. This mini-game requires you to catch a big fish using a special
articles.body:
Fishing Pond is a Mini-Game found in Lake Hylia in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. This mini-game requires you to catch a big fish using a special item, the Fishing Rod.

Check out IGN's full guide to Fishing Pond below.

Fishing Pond is a fishing mini-game in Lake Hylia. This mini-game is accessible as both Young and Adult Link. Pay 30 Rupees to start a session, then head to the water to begin. Take a second to look closely at the water and see where the biggest fish available is located.

Press ZR to aim and cast your line. Press ZR to slowly reel in, until a fish latches onto your bait. Press ZR to hook the fish, then the battle begins. You need to tilt the stick in the direction the fish is moving to wear it out. Hold ZR the whole time so that when the fish becomes tired you start reeling it in instantly.

As Young Link, catch anything over 40cm to win a Piece of Heart.

As Adult Link, catch anything over 60cm to win the Gold Scale.

You can also challenge yourself to catch the Hyrule Loach, see our detailed guide here .

articles.summary: Dampe Race is a Mini-Game found in the Lost Woods in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. This mini-game requires you to follow Dampe through a twisty
articles.body:
Dampe Race is a Mini-Game found in the Lost Woods in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. This mini-game requires you to follow Dampe through a twisty underground maze without losing your way.

Check out IGN's full guide to Dampe Race below.

Dampe Race is a mini-game found in the Kakariko Village Graveyard, as Adult Link only. Pull on the leftmost gravestone on the north side of the Graveyard to unveil the entrance to Dampe’s grave.

Once inside, speak to Dampe to start the race. To win, you need to follow Dampe to the end of the ruins. Fall too far behind, and you will lose automatically. You need to navigate a few obstacles along the way, and also avoid the purple flames Dampe throws behind him. Win the Dampe race once to receive the Hookshot. Return and do it again (under a minute) and you will win a Piece of Heart.

Up Next: Kakariko Village Shooting Gallery Mini-Game

articles.title: Dandori Academy - Pikmin 4 Guide - IGN

articles.body:
As established in the original Pikmin 4, "Dandori" is a term describing the art of efficiency -- of commanding and directing your Pikmin to the utmost level of effectiveness. Explorers in the Pikmin universe are proud of their abilities and occasionally want to put them to the test in a competitive manner.

That's the background for Dandori Academy. Imagine it like an upgraded and expanded version of the Dandori Challenges found in the game, but with a twist.

There are 72 different stages included in this new Academy mode, but they're rollout over time to create a live service game experience.

Select Dandori Academy from the Main Menu of the Pikmin 4: Nintendo Switch 2 Edition to start. You will be welcomed by the Sage Leaf, who will test players' skills in the art and craft of Dandori.

You then create a Student ID by either reusing your main Story character or customizing and then naming your character. The Student ID acts as a stamp card that shows the medals you collect in battle.

Pikmin 4 now features voice control. You can use your voice to control Oatchi with a number of commands. The feature is off by default and needs to be enabled from the Options/Settings menu.

The "Come Back" command can be very helpful in that you call just Oatchi back out of a group of Pikmin, which is helpful if you want to have him charge and stun enemies or help to destroy objects faster without disrupting the Pikmin's work.

You can play Dandori Academy anytime after completing the first three Training levels -- but there is a catch!

Dandori Academy functions as a weekly challenge mode with Exams usually* taking place over the course of a three day period that includes the weekend across all worldwide territories.

New stages are distributed on the first Monday of each month. There are a total of 12 exam periods, with six courses each.

Players can practice them any day of the week to try and achieve the highest score and medal, but on weekends, the Exam option unlocks.

When taking an exam, you gain the ability to earn Dandori points and medals and enter a leaderboard that measures your performance against other competing players. If you miss a challenge, don't worry, you can retake previous exams during the exam period. Once you've taken an exam, you can only retry it if you have a Redo Pass. These special tickets can be earned by playing the Practice mode. You can hold up to six passes.

Dandori points unlock in-game rewards, such as status displays, Pikmin Bloom gifts, icons, stamps, and frames. The game features a built-in Reward List that tells you what point levels will unlock what.

Before playing any stage, first read through the briefing on the course screen. Apart from the overall goal and the difficulty level, you will get an important hint and details about what Pikmin are present.

The most important fact, though, is Oatchi's strength for the stage, listed in the lower left corner as Pup Strength. Oatchi's strength varies between 5, 10, 30, and 100. This corresponds to the item number designations. If Oatchi's strength is 100, he can swallow and return an item with 100 weight score -- so he's got the power of 100 regular Pikmin.

Oatchi is a crucial element when trying to get the fastest times. Not only can your character and Pikmin ride him and jump over obstacles, you can assign Oatchi to retrieve items by himself. Don't just have him follow you around while you toss and charge your Pikmin at objectives. Always assign Oatchi a task!

Pull Pikmin out of the ground. Just send him to a circle of buried Pikmin and he'll save you the time of pulling them out.

Smash through pots and fungi. Hit and hold the charge command, then let Oatchi clear the path for your Pikmin.

Stun enemies. Have Oatchi attack first, then send in your little warriors.

Pull and push obstacles according to his Pup Strength.

Don't let Oatchi idle! He's your biggest asset.

Read the objectives carefully. Some missions require you to bring everything back that you can carry, but there are many challenges that have more specific goals. For example, you may only be required to collect all treasures and gold nuggets. In that case, don't waste your time on battling -- let alone carrying -- enemies.

Create a Path and Clear Things As You Go

You might not have to defeat all enemies, but do clear out enemies that are in the path of your returning Pikmin. The same goes for stage hazards, such as flame jets, fungi, or blockers such as gates, pots, and the like.

Split up your forces to work on multiple objectives at the same time. For example, have some Pikmin and/or Oatchi open up pathways while having other Pikmin carry back objects as you wait for the path to be open.

Some stages let you build up your army by smashing objects or pulling new Pikmin out of the ground. Don't go chasing them all down first. Grow your force as you venture farther from your base. Use the Practice mode to learn about stage layout -- some courses allow you to move your base, letting you clear out one side and then moving on to another.

You will encounter small objects, heavy objects, and stashes of gold. Sometimes it's better to have a single Pikmin dedicated to a pile of gold while you clear out the rest of the stage, instead of having to run back and forth to retrieve a large number of idling Pikmin that finished a job.

If you keep all Pikmin in a perpetual leaf state, you'll fall behind with each new item you pick up and carry. Use Practice mode to find spots where you get yellow Nectar that can be used to upgrade your Pikmin.

Use Everything You've Learned in Story Mode

But remember your medal and points depend on your quick completion times. Dandori Academy is about perfecting your runs. Think about speed with everything you do. Don't toss Pikmin unless you're trying to break or stomp on things -- instead, send them in fast with X to perform a charge.

But be judicious and don't overcommit your forces to single objects. The speed gains aren't that great. It's better to split up your forces and go after many things at the same time. This also ensures that you don't have to run back to base for large numbers of idle Pikmin.

Finally, remember your Pikmin's strengths and weaknesses. Elemental abilities and resilience aside, you want to make sure you bring the right Pikmin for the job. Don't have a Purple Pikmin carry a light object, but do use Rock Pikmin to stun enemies, Red Pikmin for battling, and so on.

* At launch, the exam period was extended to last from 11/12/26 to 11/15/26, so one extra day.
